title: Demo environment PRD + scope agreement (demo tenant v1)
creator: Talia Benson
dependencies: PM-184 is the scope gate for downstream ENG/DES work; no blocking dependencies.
description:
## Summary
We need a reliable, repeatable sales demo environment (“demo tenant”) with a standardized talk track + deck that any AE/SE can run with consistent outcomes.

This ticket exists to drive *scope agreement* for Demo Tenant v1: define must-have scenarios, non-functional requirements, success metrics, out-of-scope, and the milestone plan. This is the gating doc for engineering execution and enablement rollout.

## Background / problem
Recent demos have been brittle and inconsistent due to:
- quota/rate limit surprises and capacity contention during live calls
- model catalog/rollout changes changing outputs mid-demo
- auth/RBAC misconfig blocking SE access
- Console dashboards empty (no traffic / no seeded data / confusing default filters)
- no shared “backup mode” (screenshots/recording/canned outputs) for when something fails

We need a production-like tenant with synthetic workload and pinned model versions, plus automation to reset/verify the environment in minutes.

## Goals
1) Every demo (30 min default) can be run end-to-end by any certified AE/SE with a consistent happy path.
2) Demo environment is resilient to common failure modes (quota/capacity/auth/model change/dashboard empty).
3) Demo environment is safe to use: synthetic data only, least-privilege access, auditable access.
4) Supports parallel demos without cross-demo contamination.

## Non-goals (Demo Tenant v1)
- Not a customer POC tenant. (POCs will have separate processes and isolated environments.)
- Not an exhaustive tour of every Console view or every product feature.
- Not a permanent public sandbox; access is limited to internal GTM + approved partners under explicit rules.

## Primary personas + what we must show
(These map to the enablement persona doc; included here for scope clarity.)
1) App engineer / product engineer
   - “How do I integrate quickly?” Streaming chat, structured output, tool calling, retries.
2) ML platform lead / infra owner
   - “How does this run in production?” Latency/cost levers, routing/fallback, rollouts.
3) Security reviewer
   - “Is this safe to deploy?” SSO/SAML narrative, audit logs, retention, VPC/private architecture.
4) Procurement / exec sponsor
   - “What’s the business case?” predictable economics, reliability story, deployment flexibility.

## Must-have demo scenarios (v1)
### A. Core API demo (live)
- Chat completions with streaming enabled.
- Structured output (JSON schema / constrained output) with a deterministic example.
- Tool calling (one tool is enough) + tool result fed back into the model.
- Retries/backoff behavior demonstrated (or narrated) for transient errors.

**Acceptance: **SE can run a scripted example and consistently get a “clean” output within 1–2 minutes of live execution.

### B. “Production economics” demo (live)
- Show token-level latency/cost breakdown in Console.
- Demonstrate a simple lever change (e.g., batching/caching profile toggle) and narrate the tradeoff:
  - improved unit cost without blowing up latency SLO
  - or reduced latency at higher unit cost

**Acceptance:** Console shows non-empty charts for the demo project with at least:
- requests over time
- latency p50/p95
- token usage and estimated cost
- error rate

### C. Reliability / graceful degradation demo (live or semi-live)
- Route configured with a pinned model version + safe fallback policy.
- Demonstrate failover to a compatible variant/region when the preferred target is constrained.

**Acceptance:** We have a safe, repeatable way to demonstrate fallback behavior without requiring a real outage.
- Option 1 (preferred): a “simulate capacity constraint” flag in demo routing or a controlled test route.
- Option 2 (backup): pre-recorded output + screenshots with a clear narrative.

### D. Observability / operations demo (live)
- Console dashboards populated via synthetic traffic generator.
- At least one trace/error analysis example with a known “synthetic error” that is safe to show.
- Rollouts view (canary / A-B) visible with synthetic load.

**Acceptance:** There is a known-good path to show:
- a rollout timeline
- comparison metrics for two variants
- how to rollback / set fallback policy

### E. Enterprise/security demo (narrative + screenshots)
- SSO/SAML, RBAC model (roles), audit logs.
- Retention controls and data residency framing.
- Private/VPC/on-prem architecture narrative (no live provisioning required).

**Acceptance:** We have vetted screenshots and a short security FAQ link set that reps can share, with explicit do/don’t guidance.

## “Known-good” definition (demo regression policy)
A demo scenario is “known-good” when:
- the scripted steps complete successfully end-to-end
- the observed outputs match an expected-output envelope (not exact tokens, but key fields/structure)
- the Console views are populated and interpretable (no empty states)
- the steps are documented in the runbook with expected timings and at least one backup mode

A “demo regression” is any change that breaks a known-good scenario or causes the Console to appear empty/misleading during a demo.

## Demo tenant requirements
### Environment isolation + structure
- Dedicated demo org (internal-only) with clearly named projects.
- Per-demo “namespace” or project cloning strategy to avoid cross-demo contamination.
- Hard guardrails preventing reset scripts from touching non-demo tenants.

### Provisioning + reset (must be automated)
- One-command provisioning/reset that is idempotent.
- Resets complete in minutes (target: ≤10 minutes end-to-end, including verification).
- Key rotation helpers for demo-scoped keys.

### Model pinning + controlled fallback
- Pin demo routes to specific model versions.
- Define allowed fallbacks by model family and region.
- Monitor/alert on upstream catalog changes that would break pins or fallbacks.

### Synthetic traffic + seeded data
- Continuous synthetic traffic generator to keep dashboards “warm”.
- Seed prompt sets/evals and at least one error scenario.
- Ensure metrics look realistic (not a flat line), with distributions that make charts believable.

### Security constraints
- Synthetic-only data; no customer prompts, PII, or real company names.
- Least-privilege API keys per role (AE vs SE vs admin).
- Audited access to demo org; documented sharing rules.
- Any screenshots/recordings must be from the demo tenant only.

## Success metrics (v1)
- Demo setup time: < 5 minutes for SE to get ready (excluding call prep).
- Reset time: ≤10 minutes with a clear pass/fail healthcheck.
- Demo failure rate (demo-impacting issues): < 5% of demos in a month after rollout.
- “Dashboard empty” incidents: 0 in steady state (should be prevented by synthetic traffic + healthcheck).
- Certification adoption: 90% of AEs/SEs in pilot group certified within 2 weeks of rollout.

## Out of scope (explicit)
- Live Private/VPC deployment in real customer cloud accounts.
- Multi-region disaster recovery drills beyond the scripted fallback demo.
- Extensive competitive bake-offs inside the demo tenant (handled via narrative/benchmarks).
- Long-running eval pipelines for prospects (handled via POC process).

## Timeline + milestones (6–8 week plan, for planning)
Week 1: Requirements + narrative signoff
- Freeze v1 scenarios and talk track story arc
- Agree on “known-good” definition + regression ownership

Weeks 2–4: Demo tenant build
- Provisioning + reset automation
- Seed synthetic org/projects/routes/prompt sets
- Model pinning + fallback policy
- Synthetic traffic generator + dashboard sanity

Weeks 3–5: Talk track + deck
- Slide content and speaker notes
- Backup screenshots/recordings
- Timing + handoffs (AE ↔ SE)

Weeks 5–6: Internal enablement
- Training sessions
- Certification rubric and checklist
- Publish docs/runbooks + announce

Ongoing: Maintenance
- Monitoring/alerts
- Monthly scenario refresh window (controlled)
- Incident process for demo outages

## Open questions (to resolve before eng kickoff)
1) Parallel demos: do we allocate per-demo projects or per-demo API keys + routing namespaces?
2) Fallback demo: do we implement a deterministic “simulate constraint” mechanism vs rely on pre-recorded fallback artifacts?
3) Console demo surface: which views are stable enough to be in the happy path vs appendix only?
4) Data residency narrative: do we need an EMEA-specific variant for week-1 scope, or handle as a branch in talk track?

## Acceptance criteria (this ticket)
- [x] Must-have scenarios list agreed by Sales (Stephanie/Lukas), SE (Markus), PMM (Soojin).
- [x] Non-functional requirements written and agreed (reset time, parallel demos, synthetic-only, pinning).
- [x] Clear milestone plan and sub-issue breakdown created (ENG/DES/PM enablement).
- [x] Explicit out-of-scope list documented.
- [x] Security review requirement confirmed and assigned in downstream tickets.

comments: 2025-10-29 (Soojin Lee): Please ensure we explicitly define what we can claim live vs what is narrative-only. For enterprise/security, we need vetted screenshots + a short FAQ we can send without looping legal each time.
2025-10-30 (Markus Klein): +1 on backup mode. Biggest sources of demo pain have been empty Console graphs and quota surprises. Reset must be one command with a healthcheck output that’s unambiguous.

2025-10-31 (Sean Gallagher): Add demo-specific SLOs as a downstream requirement. Even if demo isn’t production, we need an escalation path and error-budget policy; otherwise the on-call handoffs will be messy.

2025-11-01 (Ethan Park): Auth/RBAC guardrails: we should enforce org name allowlist for reset commands and require short-lived elevated permissions. Also recommend keys scoped by project/role to avoid accidental misuse.

2025-11-05 (Stephanie Nguyen): Approved scope for NA. Must-have for exec demos: a crisp 3-minute ‘why Redwood’ intro and a clean economics story. Reliability/fallback can be a module unless the customer flags it early.
2025-11-06 (Lukas Meyer): For EMEA, data residency and private deployment narrative must be tight. OK to keep it as a talk-track branch for v1, but we need at least 2 slides/screenshots ready.

2025-11-20 (Talia Benson): Marking Done. Scope and must-have scenarios signed off; sub-issues created and owners assigned. Next: PM-197 to freeze known-good scenario outputs and regression policy in detail.
